# Independent review: Luna Max IGES C++

Run UID `0e6736d8-b82a-4178-bfc2-cd4245159e8d`; frozen result **231/249 (92.77%)**, IGES 1.0.21, suite `8807848`, Codex CLI 0.153.4. Raw root: `transient_results/non-rs274-oct1/iges-cpp-gpt-5.6-luna-max/iges-cpp/codex-cli/gpt-5.6-luna_max/eval1/run1` (called R below). Source references below are R/source/main.cpp. Review followed run-eval. No source was executed on the host, and raw artifacts, tests, score and publication were not changed.

## Disposition

Qualifies for publication with the frozen score and explicit caveats, subject to the parent's separate exact accounting gate. This is a substantial, successfully built implementation which completed voluntarily, not an interrupted or infrastructure-invalid run. The 18 failed observations do not represent 18 independent defects. In particular, four cases share the Type 312 reader bug and two appendices share the Type 212 numeric-type bug. Three writer cases contain a single-physical-line oracle overconstraint; two Attribute Table cases expose a missing public numeric-code table as well as the implementation's incompatible mapping. Do not adjust scoring during this collection or automatically pause on those documented caveats.

## Complete mapping of all 18 failures

All test names below refer to Evals/IGES/tests; outcomes and assertion text were checked against R/test-report.json.

1. `test_annotation_entities.py::test_new_general_note_multiple_strings_roundtrip` — Type 213 parser line 1400 groups integer fields before real fields and leaves both strings until last. Writer line 1602 emits the interleaved public schema order. Consequently the first string's `chrwid=0.7` is read as integer `font`. This is an actual writer/reader roundtrip defect, not a pointer or geometry issue. Public technical requirements Type 213 starts at line 1418.

2. `test_metadata_entities.py::test_text_display_template_roundtrip`;
   `test_pointer_backed_fields.py::test_network_subfigure_definition_display_pointer_roundtrips`;
   `test_pointer_backed_fields.py::test_network_subfigure_instance_definition_and_display_pointers_roundtrip`;
   `test_spline_and_fea_entities.py::test_connect_point_roundtrips_full_metadata_fields` — four observations of the Type 312 parsing order. Reader line 1412 reads `cbw,cbh,sl,a,xs,ys,zs` before `fc,m,vh`; writer line 1614 interleaves `fc`, `m`, `vh` as required by its own schema (technical requirements Type 312, line 1623). Direct fixture has `fc=-3` and real positions; its own output eventually presents a Real token where the reader demands an integer. The other three fixtures include supporting Text Display Templates (including DE 5, and DE 7 in the Connect Point test); their first parse fails in this support entity. Do not label all four as independent Type 132/320/420 pointer defects.

3. `test_pointer_backed_fields.py::test_nodal_results_gnote_and_np_roundtrip` and `::test_element_results_gnote_and_ep_roundtrip` — Type 146/148 readers at lines 1374–1375 read integer counts before TIME, whereas writers 1576–1577 put TIME after GNOTE and SCN. The fixture TIME values 1.5 and 2.0 therefore land in integer `nv`. Public schemas start at technical requirements 1078 and 1097. Two entity codec instances share this positional-order defect; their General Note support does not explain these failures.

4. `test_entity_roundtrips.py::test_property_roundtrip` — Type 406 parser lines 1419–1474 defaults generic form 0 values to integers; writer 1621 accepts and emits the tagged heterogeneous values. Public technical requirements 1738–1769 explicitly permit the full FieldValue union except pointers for PropertyData. Fixture `[int 42, real 3.14, string LINWIDTH]` therefore cannot read its own output. A separate read-only, network-disabled pinned-container diagnostic by the other reviewer recovered the exact first error: `invalid integer field integer`, section 2.2.2.1, physical line 8, after successful writing of `406,3,42,3.14000000000000012e+00,8HLINWIDTH;`. This is a task-contract defect, regardless of what particular standard property forms ordinarily mean.

5. `test_data_types.py::test_zero_count_hollerith_is_rejected_after_defaulted_string_control` and `test_writer_global.py::test_write_empty_document_roundtrips_default_global_values` — reader accepts and writer emits illegal `0H`. Source 528–530 writes the length without excluding zero; 606–623 explicitly allows zero. Supplied spec section 2.2.2.3, line 400, requires a nonzero count, with defaulted empty fields distinct under 2.2.3. The reader control first succeeds with a legal defaulted string; the writer assertion independently scans the complete Global payload, so matching reader/writer mistakes do not earn credit. These are genuine complementary acceptance/serialization defects, not the numeric-boundary oracle caveat.

6. `test_reference_fixtures.py::test_appendix_file_parse_and_roundtrip[ex1.iges-21]` — source 1476 requires Type 408 `scale` via rr(), rejecting an omitted defaultable final field. Supplied specification section 4.133, table at line 7748, explicitly gives scale default 1.0; section 2.2.3 also requires defaults after an early record delimiter. Isolated diagnostic recovered `missing parameter field scale`, section 2.2.2, physical line 54. This is not Luna JavaScript's DDF failure and not Terra JavaScript's numeric-boundary restriction. It is the observed first error only: later paths in the appendix were not established to be correct.

7. `test_reference_fixtures.py::test_appendix_file_parse_and_roundtrip[ex2.iges-90]` and `[ex3.iges-109]` — Type 212 reader 1399 parses `wc` and `hc` as integers, and writer 1601 also emits them with addInt. The supplied General Note table explicitly declares width and height Real (spec lines 5857–5858; JSON names wc/hc in technical requirements 1401–1402). Offline diagnostics recovered `invalid integer field wc`, section 2.2.2.1, lines 193 and 299 respectively. These two observations share one real-vs-integer codec defect; do not inherit the JavaScript missing-final-newline diagnosis. These are first-error diagnostics, not exhaustive claims about all appendix entities.

8. `test_entity_roundtrips.py::test_attribute_table_definition_form_one_roundtrip` and `test_metadata_entities.py::test_attribute_table_definition_form_two_roundtrip` — Type 322 read/write mapping at 1416/1618 uses AVDT 1=real, 2=string, 3=pointer, otherwise=int. Frozen fixtures require 2=real and 1=int, so both fail during writing with `attribute value kind does not match avdt`. Important public-documentation caveat: technical requirements 1687 names AVDT range 0–6 and 1767–1769 says it selects one of four kinds, but does not provide the numeric mapping. The supplied specification explicitly omits section 4.79 (lines 6066 and 6399). Thus record the precise compatibility failure without presenting this numeric mapping as unambiguously supplied in the frozen public docs. A future eval revision should include the authoritative AVDT mapping, including supported/unsupported values, rather than silently relying on external standards knowledge.

9. `test_writer_format.py::test_real_values_in_parameter_records_are_spec_legal`, `test_writer_param.py::test_line_parameter_record_has_entity_type_prefix_and_expected_field_count`, and `::test_parameter_records_use_selected_custom_delimiters` — three assertion observations with a test-design caveat. All inspect only `P[0][:64].rstrip()` and demand the record terminator there (writer-format helper line 46; writer-param lines 30 and 44). Source formatReal 307–315 emits long, otherwise legal scientific notation; wrapPayload 1851 and writer 1864 split a Line entity over multiple P lines. The first two fail on the partial body ending `3.0000000000`, before checking coordinate values or their lexical form. The custom-delimiter first line ends with `|` after two full nonzero coordinates, with the final coordinate and `#` on a later line. Public requirements do not require one physical line per Line entity. This is distinct from Terra's explicit `0,0` tail issue.

   Separately, this writer blindly slices both numeric and string tokens at physical widths, rather than boundary-aware packing. Section 2.2.3's numeric-end/delimiter constraint and the prompt's concatenation rule need the same careful interpretation already documented in `docs/validation/non-rs274-2026-09-12/iges-frozen-suite-followup.md`. Do not use the flawed first-line assertions as proof that the entire output is standards-compliant, or as proof of three distinct numeric/custom-delimiter defects. Future tests should gather the complete DE-owned parameter record, validate its intended semantic fields and allowed tails, and check physical numeric-boundary rules separately using an explicit contract.

Counts: 1 + 4 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 3 = 18. Thirteen observations have concrete task/spec-supported implementation causes; two have the AVDT documentation gap; three have first-line-only assertion caveats. No corrected score is proposed.

## Transcript, completion, and integrity

The transcript shows extensive local documentation/source inspection, implementation, compilation and incremental self-tests. There were recoverable compile/self-test failures and context-missing patch attempts during development; those are model work, not a premature infrastructure stop. The late successful item 371 command ends `final-check-ok`. Item 375 rebuilds, performs two sample roundtrips, byte-compares them, checks 80-column physical output and exits 0 with `final2-ok`.
